title: Topology-Driven Node-Linker Coupling Enables Exceptional Thermal and Mechanical Performance in Covalent Organic Frameworks.

screen.tldr: Topology-guided design in covalent organic frameworks yields unusually high thermal conductivity and mechanical robustness through stronger node-linker coupling.
screen.transfer_note: Topology-property relationships and structure-guided design could inform screening of mechanically robust crystalline candidates and flexible framework motifs.

title: A Novel Mechanism of Optical Spectrum Formation in the Cs2NaInCl6 Doped with Sb and Er
summary: We present a mechanism describing the formation of the optical spectrum in double halide perovskites (DHPs), specifically Sb- and Er-doped Cs2NaInCl6. Optical measurements conducted at the Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY) facility between 10 and 300 K have revealed that the bandgap of Cs2NaInCl6 is significantly larger than previously estimated, measuring 6.7 eV. Based on density-functional theory (DFT) calculations, we conclude that the formation of In+ (5s2 optical center) is crucial to the luminescence observed in Cs2NaInCl6 microcrystals produced by precipitation techniques. The formation of In+ is associated with the transfer of electron density from Cl– to In3+, which occurs due to defects in Cs2NaInCl6, resulting in increased In content. This process is linked to the self-trapped exciton mechanism and the formation of defect-trapping levels within the Cs2NaInCl6 bandgap. Additionally, embedding Sb3+ (5s2 doped ion) and Er3+ affects both the crystal structure and absorption properties of Cs2NaInCl6 samples. These findings shed light on the intricate interactions between the synthesis, composition, and the optical behavior of both undoped and Sb3+, Er3+-doped Cs2NaInCl6 powder samples.

screen.tldr: DFT and optical spectroscopy explain defect-assisted luminescence and bandgap behavior in Sb- and Er-doped Cs2NaInCl6 double halide perovskites.

title: Carbon Coking‐Tolerant Perovskite Catalyst Nd <sub>0.9</sub> Mg <sub>0.1</sub> Fe <sub>0.4</sub> Ni <sub>0.6</sub> O <su
summary: Perovskite with high temperature stability and tunability is a very promising material for dry reforming of methane (DRM), but its poor resistance to carbon coking severely limits its application. To improve the performance of catalysts in resistance to carbon coking, a common strategy is to construct active alloy structures. Here, we designed a new perovskite‐type catalyst Nd 0.9 Mg 0.1 Fe 0.4 Ni 0.6 O 3 by screening lanthanides and alkaline earth metal at the A site of perovskite and controlling the iron–nickel ratio at the B site. This catalyst exhibited excellent activity and good stability in the DRM reaction. The optimized Nd 0.9 Mg 0.1 Fe 0.4 Ni 0.6 O 3 catalyst achieved conversions of CH 4 of 93.1% and CO 2 of 94.7% at 850°C without diluent gas, and exhibited stable activity for 100 h. The good performance of Nd 0.9 Mg 0.1 Fe 0.4 Ni 0.6 O 3 material can be attributed to the formation of exsolved Fe‐Ni alloy nanoparticles with a ratio of 1:1.

screen.tldr: Perovskite catalyst design for dry reforming of methane, emphasizing coking resistance via exsolved Fe-Ni alloy nanoparticles and compositional tuning.

title: Modulating energy band structure and energy transfer pathways in CAU-10 series MOFs via ligand engineering to enhance photocatalytic oxidase-like activity for multimodal phytate detection.
summary: The photocatalytic oxidase-like activity of the CAU-10 series metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) has not been systematically investigated to date. In this study, ligand engineering was employed to precisely tune the energy band positions of CAU-10 MOFs (CAU-10-H, -OH, -Br, -NO2, -NH2, etc.) and their energy transfer pathways in photo-triggered oxidase-mimicking reactions. Results showed that CAU-10-NH2 exhibits excellent photocatalytic oxidase-like activity, which was subsequently applied to the multimodal detection of phytic acid (PA). Under UV irradiation, CAU-10-NH2 generates ROS with •OH as the predominant species at short irradiation times (10-20 s), whereas the contributions of 1O2 and •O2- become significant alongside •OH upon extending irradiation to 3 min. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that the amino group in the 5-aminoisophthalic acid ligand not only effectively regulates the valence band (VB) of the MOFs but also enhances their hydrophilicity through hydrogen bonding with water, thereby facilitating hole oxidation to generate abundant hydroxyl radicals (•OH). In contrast, although the isophthalic acid-based MOF (CAU-10-H) exhibits a suitable VB alignment, its inherently weak hydrophilicity impedes hole-water interactions, leading to the dominant radiative recombination (strong phosphorescence) and consequently negligible photocatalytic oxidase-like activity. Collectively, these results highlight how ligand engineering dictates both the photoluminescent and photocatalytic oxidase-like activity of CAU-10 MOFs. Moreover, leveraging the excellent photocatalytic oxidase-like activity of CAU-10-NH2 and the significant inhibitory effect of phytic acid (PA) on alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, a multimodal PA detection method has been developed and applied for the analysis of PA content in corn.

screen.tldr: Ligand engineering tunes CAU-10 MOF band positions, hydrophilicity, and ROS pathways to boost photocatalytic oxidase-like activity for phytate sensing.
